raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Fix rejection sampling when the draft vocabulary is smaller than the target vocabulary, in both Model Runner V1 and V2, including the V1 CPU fallback.

Fixes #61112 and #61113.

## Claims

- Recover tokens outside the draft vocabulary without padding draft tensors.
- Fix V1 draft-row indexing and preserve the full target vocabulary in V2 standard, block, and watermarked verification.

## Validation

Local CUDA tests ran on WSL with an RTX 3050 (8 GB), Python 3.12, and Torch 2.14.0+cu132, using the PR Python source with existing CUDA libraries.

- Sampler suites: **198 passed**, including **24 boundary cases** covering multiple draft positions and the 8,192-token block boundary.
- LLM/EAGLE regression: **2 passed with each sampler backend** (native and default), covering V1 and V2. Small generated checkpoints test a known target distribution; all 7,680 evaluated tokens per run stayed in its support, with frequencies within 0.035 of the expected probabilities.
- CPU fallback: **1 passed** with a source-built CPU extension, Torch 2.13.0+cpu, and `HAS_TRITON=False`.
- Applicable pre-commit checks passed.

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/sample/test_rejection_sampler.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py
VLLM_PLUGINS= VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 python -m pytest -q tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/eagle/test_eagle_correctness.py -k narrow_vocabulary
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/e2e/test_cpu_spec_decode.py::test_cpu_rejection_sampler_supports_narrow_draft_probs
```

With the sampler files reverted to `a7407ab4455`, the boundary test recovered token 0 instead of 8,200, and the V2 engine test never emitted the target-only token (expected frequency 0.2). Both pass with the fix. The engine test checks correctness with controlled weights, not trained-model quality.

The reporter also [retested the original CPU reproducer at `63184b36e88`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61152#issuecomment-6147994136): all three cases produced 0/9,898 off-support tokens. macOS/ARM remains untested.

## Details

V1 used the target vocabulary width to index draft probabilities, which could read past narrow rows. V2 truncated the target vocabulary to the draft width, dropping valid probability mass. The fix passes the draft stride and width to the kernels and treats missing draft entries as zero probability. The CPU adapters and operator schemas are updated together.

This differs from #42775, which adds model-loading and output masking support. This PR fixes sampling from narrow draft tensors already produced by the model.

---

<summary>Pull Request Checklist</summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill.
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] **Design Fit:** Keeps the fix within the existing sampling paths.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Includes kernel, CPU fallback, and engine regressions with local validation.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Applicable pre-commit checks passed.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes the root cause, related issues, and test results.

</details>

nodes.body: Hey @SeverinVisionary could you rerun the original macOS C++ and triton-cpu reproducers, plus the narrow EAGLE end-to-end case if feasible? I only have CUDA hardware.

Thanks @maithilijoshi20. I reran the original N7 C++ reproducer on Linux x86-64, with `--device cpu --batches 20`, using separate CPU builds of `bfa7e5b7a` and `5a79873df`. Both used Torch 2.13.0+cpu and the genuine C++ fallback (`HAS_TRITON=False`).

On the parent, the padded control emitted 0/9,898 tokens outside the target support; the narrow and narrow_m1 cases each emitted 3,345/9,898. On the PR head, the first padded-control call failed before returning a result:

```text
RuntimeError: _C::sample_recovered_tokens_kernel_impl() Expected a value of type 'Tensor' for argument 'target_probs' but instead found type 'int'.
Position: 4
Value: 50257
```

This looks like an argument-order mismatch in the CPU override. `sample_recovered_tokens_kernel` puts `draft_probs_stride` immediately after `draft_probs`, while `_sample_recovered_tokens_kernel_impl` puts it after `vocab_size`. `KernelOverride._launch` forwards in the original kernel's order, so the padded stride, 50257, reaches `target_probs`. The same ordering difference appears in the random-rejection CPU override too.

I kept that first failure without patching or rerunning the arm. The remaining fix cases, triton-cpu and EAGLE checks did not run, so I can't confirm the full fix yet. macOS remains untested.

AI assistance was used for the retest, evidence review and this write-up.

Thanks, @SeverinVisionary. The CPU override argument ordering is fixed, and the regression now launches through KernelOverride before reaching the genuine C++ fallback. Locally, it passes with HAS_TRITON=False.
If possible, could you rerun the original N7 C++ reproducer with --device cpu --batches 20 against the current head?

Thanks @maithilijoshi20. I reran the unchanged original N7 reproducer with `--device cpu --batches 20` at `63184b36e8830e2b67b215313047e1e797a24fa2`.

On Linux x86_64 with Torch 2.13.0+cpu, genuine `HAS_TRITON=False` and the production `KernelOverride`/C++ path, it exited 0. The padded argument-type error from my earlier run at `5a79873` did not recur. All three cases—`padded`, `narrow` and `narrow_m1`—reported 0/9,898 off-support emitted tokens. Each case printed rounded first-token frequencies `a=.504, b=.286, c=.210, other=0`, against the toy target law `.5/.3/.2`. These finite observations do not establish statistical exactness or token-for-token equality between cases.

This used the exact new Python source with the retained source-built native libraries from `5a79873`. I checked the complete direct source-tree comparison: only the CPU Python adapter and regression test changed; the native/build inputs and operator ABI are unchanged. This is a component retest, rather than a fresh full-head distribution build.

I also attempted `test_cpu_rejection_sampler_supports_narrow_draft_probs` once. Pytest stopped while importing `tests/conftest.py` because `tblib` is missing: zero tests collected or executed. macOS/ARM, genuine triton-cpu V1/V2, EAGLE and engine/model generation remain untested in this follow-up.

AI assistance was used for the retest, evidence review and this write-up.

@@ -170,3 +170,88 @@ def test_eagle_correctness_medium(
         attn_backend,
         vllm_runner,
     )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("use_v2", ["0", "1"])
+def test_eagle_narrow_vocabulary_preserves_target_distribution(
+    tmp_path, monkeypatch, vllm_runner, use_v2: str
+):
+    """Loaded EAGLE weights must preserve target-only mass during verification."""
+    import torch
+    from safetensors.torch import save_file
+    from transformers import LlamaConfig, LlamaForCausalLM
+
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER", use_v2)
+    vocab_size, draft_vocab_size, hidden_size = 8201, 8193, 64
+    config = LlamaConfig(
+        vocab_size=vocab_size,
+        hidden_size=hidden_size,
+        intermediate_size=128,
+        num_hidden_layers=2,
+        num_attention_heads=2,
+        num_key_value_heads=2,
+        max_position_embeddings=256,
+        tie_word_embeddings=False,
+    )
+    target = LlamaForCausalLM(config)
+    support = [0, 1, vocab_size - 1]
+    probabilities = [0.5, 0.3, 0.2]
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        for parameter in target.parameters():
+            parameter.zero_()
+        target.model.embed_tokens.weight.fill_(1)
+        target.model.norm.weight.fill_(1)
+        target.lm_head.weight.fill_(-1)
+        for token, probability in zip(support, probabilities):
+            target.lm_head.weight[token].fill_(
+                torch.log(torch.tensor(probability)).item() / hidden_size
+            )
+    target_path, draft_path = tmp_path / "target", tmp_path / "draft"
+    target.save_pretrained(target_path)
+    config.num_hidden_layers = 1
+    config.vocab_size = draft_vocab_size
+    config.architectures = ["EagleLlamaForCausalLM"]
+    config.save_pretrained(draft_path)
+    weights = {
+        name.removeprefix("model."): value.contiguous()
+        for name, value in target.state_dict().items()
+        if name.startswith("model.layers.0.") and "input_layernorm" not in name
+    }
+    # The EAGLE head shares target embeddings/lm_head, but truncates its logits.
+    weights["fc.weight"] = torch.cat(
+        [torch.eye(hidden_size), torch.zeros(hidden_size, hidden_size)], dim=1
+    )
+    save_file(weights, draft_path / "model.safetensors")
+
+    with vllm_runner(
+        str(target_path),
+        skip_tokenizer_init=True,
+        dtype="float32",
+        enforce_eager=True,
+        max_model_len=128,
+        max_num_seqs=32,
+        gpu_memory_utilization=0.45,
+        enable_prefix_caching=False,
+        attention_config={"backend": "TRITON_ATTN"},
+        speculative_config={
+            "method": "eagle",
+            "model": str(draft_path),
+            "num_speculative_tokens": 3,
+            "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic",
+        },
+    ) as runner:
+        outputs = runner.llm.generate(
+            [{"prompt_token_ids": [0, 1, 0]} for _ in range(512)],
+            [
+                SamplingParams(temperature=1, max_tokens=16, ignore_eos=True, seed=i)
+                for i in range(512)
+            ],
+        )
+    # Exclude the first token, which is sampled before speculative verification.
+    tokens = torch.tensor([t for o in outputs for t in o.outputs[0].token_ids[1:]])
+    assert tokens.numel() == 512 * 15
+    assert torch.isin(tokens, torch.tensor(support)).all()
+    observed = torch.stack([(tokens == token).float().mean() for token in support])
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        observed, torch.tensor(probabilities), atol=0.035, rtol=0
+    )

+    draft_logits[torch.arange(num_steps), draft_ids] = 0.0

+    target_logits[rejected_step] = float("-inf")
+    target_logits[rejected_step, -1] = 0.0
+    inputs = _build_rejection_sample_inputs(
+        target_logits[0], draft_logits[0], num_steps, 1.0, num_trials
+    )
+    inputs["target_logits"] = target_logits.repeat(num_trials, 1)
+    inputs["draft_sampled"].view(num_trials, num_steps + 1)[:, 1:] = draft_ids

+    assert (sampled[:, rejected_step] == vocab_size - 1).all()
+    assert torch.equal(

+    )

issue_comments.body: Hey @SeverinVisionary could you rerun the original macOS C++ and triton-cpu reproducers, plus the narrow EAGLE end-to-end case if feasible? I only have CUDA hardware.

Thanks @maithilijoshi20. I reran the original N7 C++ reproducer on Linux x86-64, with `--device cpu --batches 20`, using separate CPU builds of `bfa7e5b7a` and `5a79873df`. Both used Torch 2.13.0+cpu and the genuine C++ fallback (`HAS_TRITON=False`).

On the parent, the padded control emitted 0/9,898 tokens outside the target support; the narrow and narrow_m1 cases each emitted 3,345/9,898. On the PR head, the first padded-control call failed before returning a result:

```text
RuntimeError: _C::sample_recovered_tokens_kernel_impl() Expected a value of type 'Tensor' for argument 'target_probs' but instead found type 'int'.
Position: 4
Value: 50257
```

This looks like an argument-order mismatch in the CPU override. `sample_recovered_tokens_kernel` puts `draft_probs_stride` immediately after `draft_probs`, while `_sample_recovered_tokens_kernel_impl` puts it after `vocab_size`. `KernelOverride._launch` forwards in the original kernel's order, so the padded stride, 50257, reaches `target_probs`. The same ordering difference appears in the random-rejection CPU override too.

I kept that first failure without patching or rerunning the arm. The remaining fix cases, triton-cpu and EAGLE checks did not run, so I can't confirm the full fix yet. macOS remains untested.

AI assistance was used for the retest, evidence review and this write-up.

Thanks, @SeverinVisionary. The CPU override argument ordering is fixed, and the regression now launches through KernelOverride before reaching the genuine C++ fallback. Locally, it passes with HAS_TRITON=False.
If possible, could you rerun the original N7 C++ reproducer with --device cpu --batches 20 against the current head?

Thanks @maithilijoshi20. I reran the unchanged original N7 reproducer with `--device cpu --batches 20` at `63184b36e8830e2b67b215313047e1e797a24fa2`.

On Linux x86_64 with Torch 2.13.0+cpu, genuine `HAS_TRITON=False` and the production `KernelOverride`/C++ path, it exited 0. The padded argument-type error from my earlier run at `5a79873` did not recur. All three cases—`padded`, `narrow` and `narrow_m1`—reported 0/9,898 off-support emitted tokens. Each case printed rounded first-token frequencies `a=.504, b=.286, c=.210, other=0`, against the toy target law `.5/.3/.2`. These finite observations do not establish statistical exactness or token-for-token equality between cases.

This used the exact new Python source with the retained source-built native libraries from `5a79873`. I checked the complete direct source-tree comparison: only the CPU Python adapter and regression test changed; the native/build inputs and operator ABI are unchanged. This is a component retest, rather than a fresh full-head distribution build.

I also attempted `test_cpu_rejection_sampler_supports_narrow_draft_probs` once. Pytest stopped while importing `tests/conftest.py` because `tblib` is missing: zero tests collected or executed. macOS/ARM, genuine triton-cpu V1/V2, EAGLE and engine/model generation remain untested in this follow-up.
